text:
[LGRA.22.7] **Two disjoint namespaces, selected by position.** With case removed,
a schema, a constant, and a binding may share one NFC name. The compiler must
resolve a `NAME` against exactly one of two disjoint namespaces, chosen by
grammatical position:

- The **type namespace** — the builtin types, which are the rows of [LGRA.22.8],
  unit symbols, dimension and scalar-group names ([LUNI.7.1]), schemas, and the
  kind `Schema`, which is admissible only as a service kwarg's declared type ([LADP.8.6.1]) and names a fact of any schema. It is
  used at every *type position*: a `slot: T` annotation, a `let x: T` annotation,
  a `::T` cast target ([LCST.4]), and a unit literal. **Every type position lexes
  the single `TYPE_SYM` terminal** ([LGRA.2.5.3], [LCST.4.1.2]) — the type-symbol
  class (`XID` ∪ the non-`XID` unit glyphs) — so a unit type spelled with a
  non-`XID` glyph (`slot: °C`, `x::°C`) is admitted uniformly. **Units are
  types** — a unit-typed value's static kind *is* its unit symbol — so the type
  namespace is one lattice, not a type track plus a parallel unit track.
  `Bytes` is a scalar builtin at **every** type position — a `slot: T` annotation
  (`slot: Bytes`), a `let x: T` annotation, and a `::T` cast target — like the other
  scalars, with no slot carve-out.
- The **value namespace** — pattern bindings, `let` bindings, and constants. It
  is used at expression positions.

Because the two namespaces are disjoint and position-selected, a constant named
`Float` (value namespace) does not shadow the type `Float` (type namespace), and
a `::Float` cast target resolves `Float` in the type namespace only.

**The type namespace is flat:** two type-namespace entries — any of schema, unit,
dimension, scalar group or builtin — that share one NFC name are a compile error; a schema and a unit may
not both be named `celsius`. Two schemas are `DS_VALIDATE_DUPLICATE_SCHEMA`; a
schema and a unit are `DS_VALIDATE_DUPLICATE_TYPE_NAME`. A declaration taking a
builtin's name is refused as a reserved word before it can collide ([LLEX.9.7]).

Within the value namespace the compiler must resolve an expression `NAME` in the
order in-scope binding → constant → builtin function ([LEXP.17.2]); an unresolved
`NAME` is a compile error: `DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` where it is called,
a library's member included, `DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_QUALIFIED_CONST` where it is a
library's member that is not called, `DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_CONST` where it names
an entry of the type namespace, and `DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_BINDING` otherwise. A dotted name resolves by [LGRA.22.9].

**Which names an author may not declare is not this clause's to say.** The
builtin type names, the kind `Schema` and the builtin function names are
reserved words carrying rows on [LLEX.9.6], and [LLEX.9.5] is the rule that refuses them. This clause
states only how a `NAME` **resolves** once written.

The resolution order above is why the builtin function names are on that list
rather than free. A binding or constant is resolved before a builtin, so a name
left available would not merely coexist with the builtin it spells — it would
precede it, and shadow it at every call site in scope.

alloy.name: lgra_22_7__schema_kind
alloy.note: The kind Schema as one entry of the type namespace, beside the builtin types and not among them: it has no row on LGRA.22.8.

alloy.name: lgra_22_7__schema_kind_reserved_not_builtin
alloy.note: The kind's name is a reserved word (its type row on LLEX.9.6) and is none of the builtin type names.

alloy.name: lgra_22_7__schema_kind_resolves_alone
alloy.note: No builtin type and no declared type shares the kind's name. The two facts about the kind restated; fails if either the not-in-builtins line or the flat namespace's kind line is removed.
